messages.content: Identify the number of the mitochondria in a cell.

message.content:
The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands. In most mammalian cells you’ll find:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| **Red blood cells** (which lack mitochondria) | 0 |
| **Neurons** (high energy demand) | 1 000–10 000 per cell |
| **Muscle cells** (especially cardiac and skeletal muscle) | 5 000–20 000 per cell |
| **Liver hepatocytes** | 1 000–5 000 per cell |
| **Epithelial cells** (e.g., intestinal) | 200–1 000 per cell |
| **Stem cells** (low metabolic activity) | 100–500 per cell |
| **Typical fibroblast or cultured cell line** | 200–1 000 per cell |

These numbers are approximate averages; individual cells can differ by an order of magnitude. The key point is that cells with high energy requirements (neurons, muscle, liver) contain many more mitochondria than cells with lower metabolic needs.
